question: Why did Jeremy Bentham call every punishment, even a fully deserved one, an evil in itself?
answer: Because it inflicts pain, and pain is bad whoever feels it. Bentham held that punishment is justified only when it prevents a greater harm, and never where it would be groundless, ineffective, too costly or needless. A sentence that deters and reforms no one is, on his count, a second harm.
move: Count the cost of a penalty as carefully as the cost of the offence.
ask: When I punish someone, even with silence, what greater harm am I actually preventing?
source: Bentham, Principles of Morals and Legislation, ch. 13
reference: Bentham, An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation, ed. Burns & Hart, Clarendon Press, 1996, chapter 13
